Definition: Shema, the name of a place in Palestine and of four Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Shema is the name of three men and a town: a son of Hebron, a son of Joel who dwelt in Aroer, and a man who stood beside Ezra on the pulpit of wood when the law was read. The town of Shema lies in the south of Judah, listed with Amam and Moladah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the man who stood beside Ezra is the Shema to remember. He stood while the law was read to the returned people, and I hold that standing beside the reading of God's word is honour enough.
